2020.question:
Has the State promulgated
legislation (primary aviation
legislation or regulations)
permitting, as the State conducting
the investigation, the participation
of accredited representatives from
other States involved?
2020.guidance:
1) Review legislation (primary aviation
legislation or regulations).
2) Verify the particular situation in the
State regarding judicial investigations,
and its impact on the capacity of the State
to comply with Annex 13.


3) Confirm that the participation of
accredited representatives from the
following States is permitted:

a) State of Registry,

b) State of Operator,

c) State of Design,

d) State of Manufacture, and

e) Any other State which, on request,
provides information, facilities or
experts.

4) The entitlement must include the
following:

a) Visit the scene of the accident.

b) Examine the wreckage.

c) Obtain witness information and
suggest areas of questioning.

d) Have full access to all relevant
evidence as soon as possible.
e) Receive copies of all pertinent
documents.

f) Participate in read-outs of
recorded media.

g) Participate in off-scene
investigative activities, such as
component examinations, technical
briefings, tests and simulations.

h) Participate in investigation
progress meetings, including
deliberations related to analyses,
findings, causes, contributing factors and
safety recommendations.

i) Make submissions of the various
elements of the investigation.

2024_rev1.question:
Has the State promulgated specific
operating regulations to require
approved training organizations
(ATOs) to implement a safety
management system (SMS)?

Does the State ensure that the
personnel responsible for the
acceptance and continuous
surveillance of ATOs SMS are
qualified to perform their functions
and responsibilities?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that:
1) the State has identified competency requirements
for personnel responsible for the acceptance and
continuous surveillance of an SMS;
2) the content of the training programme addresses
the SMS framework elements contained in
Appendix 2 to Annex 19;
3) the training includes (but is not limited to) the
following:
a) evaluation and acceptance of an ATO’s SMS;
b) evaluation and acceptance of an ATO’s safety
performance indicators (SPIs);
c) continuous surveillance of the ATO’s SMS in a
safety management environment;
d) hazard identification and risk management
processes and methodologies;
e) protection of safety data, safety information and
related sources;
f) enforcement under the framework of SMS; and
g) soft skills (e.g. effective communication skills,
negotiation skills, conflict resolution, etc.);
4) a training plan has been implemented;
5) initial, OJT and recurrent training, as applicable,
with specified-time periods are included; and
6) training records are systematically retained.

Notes to the auditor:
1) The framework components and elements in
Appendix 2 to Annex 19 are listed in PQ 3.901.
2) This PQ is only applicable to approved training
organizations (ATOs) in accordance with Annex 1
that are exposed to safety risks related to aircraft
operations during the provision of their services.

validity;

diagrams.

procedures ensure that an operations manual has
the following components:

 b) aircraft operating information;
c) routes and aerodromes; and

training.

production approval in the absence of a
production certificate or production
organization approval?

following requirements for the manufacturer:

inspection system;

the system and

3) marking of each product and part in accordance with

by the CAA.

2024_rev1.question:
Has the State promulgated specific
operating regulations to require approved
maintenance organizations (AMOs) to
implement a safety management system
(SMS)?

Does the State ensure that the personnel
responsible for the acceptance and
continuous surveillance of AMOs SMS
are qualified to perform their functions
and responsibilities?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that:
1) the State has identified competency requirements for
personnel responsible for the acceptance and
continuous surveillance of an SMS;
2) the content of the training programme addresses the
SMS framework elements contained in Appendix 2 to
Annex 19;
3) the training also includes (but is not limited to) the
following:
a) evaluation and acceptance of an AMO’s SMS;
b) evaluation and acceptance of an AMO’s safety
performance indicators (SPIs);
c) continuous surveillance of the AMO’s SMS in a
safety management environment;
d) hazard identification and risk management processes
and methodologies;
e) protection of safety data, safety information and
related sources;
f) enforcement under the framework of SMS; and
g) soft skills (e.g. effective communication skills,
negotiation skills, conflict resolution, etc.);
4) a training plan has been implemented;
5) initial, OJT and recurrent training, as applicable,
with specified-time periods are included; and
6) training records are systematically retained.
Notes to the auditor:
1) The framework components and elements in
Appendix 2 to Annex 19 are addresses in PQ 5.901.
2) This PQ is only applicable to approved maintenance
organizations (AMOs) providing services to operators
of aeroplanes or helicopters engaged in international
commercial air transport.

identify hazards, assess identified safety
risks, and mitigate them appropriately?

products or services;

mitigates them appropriately.
Notes to the auditor:

industry visit.

commercial air transport.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure that safety
performance indicators and targets
established by AMOs are acceptable to
the State?
2024_rev1.guidance:
1) Review the State’s mechanism for accepting
individual AMOs safety performance indicators (SPIs)
and targets (when applicable) to verify that proposed
SPIs and respective targets (as applicable), are
developed in a manner that supports the effort to meet
their safety objectives, are formulated in a manner to
ensure that they are specific, measurable, achievable,
relevant and timebound.

proposed SPIs are reviewed and accepted as part of the
SMS acceptance.
Notes to the auditor:

implementation process.
2) This verification needs to be reviewed during the
industry visit.

organizations (AMOs) providing services to operators
of aeroplanes or helicopters engaged in international
commercial air transport.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure the AMOs monitor
their safety performance?
2024_rev1.guidance:

mechanism to ensure that the AMOs periodically
review their safety performance including the means to:
1) validate the effectiveness of safety risks controls;
2) validate the identification of changes that may affect
the level of safety risks associated with their aviation
products or services; and
3) validate the identification and management of the
safety risks that may arise from those changes.

any future investigations.
4) Records in the custody or control of
the accident investigation authority that
are to be protected include:
a) cockpit voice recordings and airborne
image recordings and any transcripts
from such recordings;
b) records from interviews with persons
by the investigation authorities in the
course of the investigation

;
c) communications between persons
having been involved in the operation of
the aircraft

;
d) medical or private information
regarding persons involved in the
accident or incident

;
e) recordings and transcripts of
recordings from air traffic control units

;
f) analysis of and opinions about
information (including flight recorder
information) made by the accident
investigation authority and accredited
representatives in relation to the accident
or incident; and


g) the draft final report of an
accident or incident investigation.

implemented means to ensure:


a) the cooperation between the
accident investigation authority
and the judicial authorities, so that
an investigation is not impeded by
administrative or judicial
investigations or proceedings; and


b) separation between the
investigation conducted under
Annex 13 and the one by the
judicial authority?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Review effective implementation of
legislation/regulations and/or formal
arrangements, if any.



Examples: Memorandums of
Understanding (MOUs) related to
coordination of activities related to:
access to the site of the accident;
preservation of and access to the
evidence; identification of victims; flight
recorder read-outs, examinations of
relevant material/evidence; initial and
ongoing debriefings of the status of each
process; exchange of information;
appropriate use of safety information;
and resolution of conflicts.

2024_rev1.question:
Has the State established and
implemented procedures to ensure
the timely recovery and effective
read-out of the flight recorders in
compliance with Attachment D to
Annex 13?
2024_rev1.guidance:
1) Verify procedures for recovery and
handling of recorders, including damaged
recorders and recorders recovered from
water.


2) Verify that the recovery and/or read-
out are not impeded or delayed for:


a) administrative reasons (e.g. senior
management or IIC may feel that it is
necessary for the IIC to be present at all
investigative activities and therefore
delay recorder read-out until on-site
documentation is complete);
b) judicial reasons (apprehensions about
chain of custody or the need to delay
readout until judicial authorities
determine their role and plan); or


c) financial reasons (inability of staff to
initiate readout without high level travel
or funding approval).


3) For underwater recovery, verify that
the State has established and
implemented a clear plan for initiating,
funding, and overseeing underwater
recovery and how these aspects will be
conducted.


4) Verify that the procedures cover not
only the choice of the read-out facility,
but also the mode of participation of the
State of Design/Manufacture and the
State of the Operator in the flight
recorder read-out and analysis activities.

2024_rev1.question:
Has the State promulgated specific
operating regulations to require operators
of certified aerodromes (aerodrome
operators) to implement a safety
management system (SMS)?

Does the State ensure that the personnel
responsible for the acceptance and
continuous surveillance of aerodrome
operators SMS are qualified to perform
their functions and responsibilities?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that:
1) the State has identified competency requirements
for personnel responsible for the acceptance and
continuous surveillance of an SMS;
2) the content of the training programme addresses
the SMS framework elements contained in
Appendix 2 to Annex 19; and
3) the training also includes (but not limited to) the
following:
  a) evaluation and acceptance of an aerodrome
operators’ SMS;
  b) evaluation and acceptance of an aerodrome
operators’ SPIs;
  c) continuous surveillance of the aerodrome
operators’ SMS in a safety management
environment;
  d) hazard identification and risk management
processes and methodologies;
  e) protection of safety data, safety information and
related sources;
  f) enforcement under the framework of SMS; and
  g) soft skills (e.g. effective communication skills,
negotiation skills, conflict resolution, etc.);

4)  a training plan has been implemented;
5) initial, OJT and recurrent training, as applicable,
with specified-time periods are included; and
6) training records are systematically retained.

Note to the auditor:
The framework components and elements in
Appendix 2 to Annex 19 addressed are listed in PQ
8.901.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure that the aerodrome
operators identify hazards, assess
identified safety risks, and mitigate them
appropriately?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that the State ensures the aerodrome
operators:
1) maintain a process to:
  a) identify hazards associated with their aviation
products or services;
  b) assess safety risks; and
  c) mitigate safety risks; and
2) actively identify hazards, assess safety risks and
mitigates them appropriately.

Note to the auditor:
This verification needs to be reviewed during the
industry visit.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure that safety
performance indicators and targets
established by aerodrome operators are
acceptable to the State?
2024_rev1.guidance:
1) Review the State’s mechanism for accepting
individual aerodrome operators’ safety performance
indicators (SPIs) and targets (when applicable) to
verify that proposed SPIs and respective targets (as
applicable), are developed in a manner that supports
the effort to meet their safety objectives, and are
formulated in a manner to ensure that they are
specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and
timebound.
2) Verify that the State ensures that the aerodrome
operators’ proposed SPIs are reviewed and accepted
as part of the SMS acceptance.

Notes to the auditor:
1) SPIs acceptance may also be done later in the
implementation process.
2) This verification needs to be reviewed during the
industry visit.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure the aerodrome
operators monitor their safety
performance?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that the State has established and
implemented a mechanism to ensure that the
aerodrome operators periodically review their safety
performance including the means to:
1) validate the effectiveness of safety risks controls;
2) validate the identification of changes that may
affect the level of safety risks associated with their
aviation products or services; and
3) validate the identification and management of the
safety risks that may arise from those changes.

aerodrome operators’ personnel involved in SMS
are qualified to perform their functions and
responsibilities; and
2) Sample surveillance activities records.

Note to the auditor:

involvement in the SMS.
2) Review the training records of the aerodrome
operators’ personnel during the industry visit.

2024_rev1.question:
Does the State ensure that the aerodrome
operators continually promote safety?
2024_rev1.guidance:
Verify that the State ensures the aerodrome

2024_rev1.question: Has the State documented the functions and activities for the establishment and maintenance of the SSP?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that the State has published SSP related documentation that outlines the functions and activities to support the implementation of its SSP, including all SSP components and associated programmes.

2024_rev1.question: Has the State designated the authority in charge of coordinating the establishment and maintenance of the SSP?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that the State:1. has formally designated the authority in charge of coordinating the implementation and maintenance of the SSP; and2. has defined and documented responsibilities and roles of the State authority in charge of coordinating the implementation and maintenance of the SSP.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State ensure that the responsibilities of the relevant State authorities regarding the SSP functions and activities are identified and defined, and that these authorities are involved in the implementation and maintenance of the SSP?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has identified and defined the roles and responsibilities related to the management of safety of each relevant State authorities (e.g. Civil Aviation Authority, Accident Investigation Authority and Military Aviation Authority and other authorities as applicable) involved in the SSP establishment and maintenance with no gaps or overlaps;2. the State has established a mechanism that facilitates the coordination of SSP related aspects at the State level, chaired by the designated authority in charge of coordinating the SSP implementation and maintenance; and3. all relevant State authorities are represented and participate in the SSP implementation and maintenance efforts.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State ensure that personnel of the State authorities involved in SSP establishment and maintenance are qualified to perform their functions and responsibilities?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State authorities have determined the SSP-related training needs for personnel involved in the SSP establishment and maintenance; 2. an SSP-related training programme has been developed for personnel involved in the SSP establishment and maintenance;3. an SSP-related training plan has been developed and implemented for personnel involved in the SSP establishment and maintenance; and 4. an SSP-related recurrent training is included to ensure that competency is retained.Note to the auditor:  This PQ excludes inspectors’ SMS qualifications, which are audited under a different set of PQs.

2024_rev1.question: Has the State established and published its safety policy which is periodically reviewed, and amended as needed?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has established its safety policy;2. the safety policy includes:    a) a clear high-level management commitment to safety, including the allocation of resources, on behalf of the relevant State authorities;    b) endorsement by all relevant State authorities who participate in the implementation and maintenance of the SSP; and    c) the need to promote positive safety culture, including an emphasis on measures to be taken to encourage safety reporting (e.g. the protection of safety data, safety information and related sources); and3. the safety policy is published and communicated, reviewed periodically, and amended as needed.

2024_rev1.question: Has the State established its safety objectives that address the State’s highest safety risk and are published, periodically reviewed and amended as needed?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has established its State safety objectives;2. the State safety objectives represent the State’s highest safety risks; and 3. the State safety objectives are published, reviewed periodically, and amended as needed.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State ensure that its safety performance indicators (SPIs) are established and monitored, to support achieving its safety objectives?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has a mechanism to select SPIs to monitor that its SSP functions and activities are achieving the intended safety objectives;2. the SPIs encompass both operational safety risks and process implementation risks;3. the SPIs and respective targets (as applicable), are developed in a manner that supports the effort to meet their safety objectives, and together, they are formulated in a manner to ensure that they are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and timebound; and4. the SPIs, targets and alert levels, when used, are periodically reviewed and amended as needed.

2024_rev1.question: Has the State established and implemented a State-level mandatory reporting system?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that the State has legislation, regulations, procedures, and a mechanism to establish and implement mandatory reporting system(s).Note to the auditor:The mandatory reporting system in this PQ is not limited to accident/incident reporting system that is assessed in AIG PQ 6.501

2024_rev1.question: Does the State ensure that safety data captured by, and safety information derived from the mandatory reporting system(s) and its related sources are protected?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has a mechanism in place to protect safety data, safety information and related sources including exceptions and agreements between State authorities as applicable; and2. the State does not make available or use safety data or safety information collected, stored, or analysed for purposes other than maintaining or improving safety, unless the competent authority determines that a principle of exception applies.
2024_rev1.references: STDA195.3.3 RPA195.3.2GMDoc 9859 Ch. 7

2024_rev1.question: Has the State established and implemented a State-level voluntary reporting system?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that the State has legislation, regulations, procedures, and mechanism to establish and implement voluntary reporting system(s).

2024_rev1.question: Does the State ensure that safety data captured by, and safety information derived from the voluntary reporting system(s) and its related sources are protected?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. the State has a mechanism to protect safety data, safety information and related sources including exceptions and agreements between State authorities as applicable; and2. the State does not make available or use safety data or safety information collected, stored, or analysed for purposes other than maintaining or improving safety, unless the competent authority determines that a principle of exception applies.

2024_rev1.question: Has the State established Safety Data Collection and Processing Systems (SDCPS) to enable safety data and information analysis?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that:1. there is a mechanism established and implemented to ensure the collection, processing and analysis of safety data and safety information at the State level;2. the sources of safety data and safety information include, but are not limited to, data and information derived from: accident and incident investigations, mandatory safety reporting systems, voluntary safety reporting systems and results of surveillance activities. Other sources may include sector-specific and self-disclosure reporting;3. the safety database(s) at the State level are categorized using an agreed upon taxonomy and supporting definitions, in a way that enables analysis of safety data and facilitates sharing and exchange of the safety information; and4. the SDCPS is accessible (or on request, considering the protection of safety data and safety information) by different relevant State authorities to support their functions and activities related to SSP establishment and maintenance. Note to the auditor: This PQ is to "enable analysis" not to perform analysis.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State identify hazards and perform safety risk assessment from the collected safety data and safety information?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that there is a mechanism established and implemented to:1. identify hazards from collected safety data and safety information; and2. perform safety risk assessments including assessment of probability, severity, and tolerability of the safety risks.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State take action on identified safety risks as required?
2024_rev1.guidance: 1. Verify that there is a mechanism established and implemented to develop, document, and take appropriate safety risk mitigation/control actions as required, at the State level.2. Sample evidence of safety risk mitigation and control actions at the State level.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State evaluate the effectiveness of actions taken to manage safety risks?
2024_rev1.guidance: 1. Verify that the State has a mechanism to assess the effectiveness of actions taken.2. Verify that the State assesses the effectiveness of actions taken to manage safety risks and to mitigate these risks to an acceptable level.3. Sample cases of actions taken. Note to the auditor: Sampling to include initial actions taken that were sufficient in lowering the risk to an acceptable level and no additional actions were required, and cases in which initial actions taken were not sufficient and additional actions were taken to ensure that the risk became acceptable.

2024_rev1.question: Does the State promote safety awareness and share safety information?
2024_rev1.guidance: Verify that the State promotes safety awareness (e.g. training, seminars, workshops), including promotion of safety reporting:1. amongst the relevant State authorities; and2. with the aviation community (e.g. service providers, aviation industry, aviation personnel).

guidance.got:
Verify that:

1) the primary aviation legislation,
specific operating regulations and/or
policies establish family assistance plans
that address the scope, responsibilities,
roles and coordination necessary to
provide assistance to aircraft accident
victims and their families

;
2) the State has ensured that air operators
and aerodrome operators have
established family assistance plans

;
3) the family assistance plans are
periodically reviewed by the State and
service providers

;
4) the State has ensured that air operators
have arrangements with aerodromes in
which they operate to implement the
family assistance plans

; and5) an agency is designated to
coordinate the timely and appropriate
delivery of assistance.
